description: Generate a slide-deck-quality RACI matrix (responsibility assignment matrix): tasks or deliverables as rows, roles or teams as columns, and each cell a rounded letter chip, R Responsible, A Accountable, C Consulted or I Informed, with "A/R" for an owner who also does the work and `model: "RASCI"` adding S for Support. Rows can be grouped into phases with `type: "section"` rows; a legend explains the letters. With `checks` (default on), tasks without exactly one A or without an R get an amber note at the row end ("No A", "2 As", "No R") and every broken rule is returned in `warnings`; give every task exactly one A and at least one R unless the user's data says otherwise. Choose it for project roles and responsibilities, PMO governance, onboarding and handover plans, and any "who does what" slide; use a Harvey ball matrix instead to score options against criteria, an org chart for reporting lines, and a timeline when the point is when work happens. Limits: 1–10 roles and up to 30 rows (tasks plus sections); keep task names to a short verb phrase and roles to a job title. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

inputSchema.description: A RACI (or RASCI) responsibility matrix: tasks or deliverables as rows, roles as columns, each cell R, A, C, I (or S), with optional phase sections and rule checks.

checks.description: Check the RACI rules: every task has exactly one A and at least one R (A/R counts as both), and every role is R or A on some task. Tasks that break a rule get an amber dot and a short note ("No A", "2 As", "No R") at the row end, and every broken rule is listed in `warnings`. Default true; set false to hide the notes.

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

legend.description: Show a legend row under the matrix explaining each letter. Default true.

model.description: "RACI" (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) or "RASCI", which adds S for Support. Sets the legend and the builder's click cycle; an S in a RACI chart is still drawn and added to the legend. Default "RACI".

palette.description: Hex colours: the first fills R chips, the second tints C chips, the third tints S chips (A is always dark and I light gray, so the letters stay distinct). Pass the user's brand colours here when they name them.

roles.description: Column headings, left to right: the roles, teams or people, e.g. ["Project manager", "Dev lead", "Design", "Legal"]. 1–10 roles, up to 30 characters each; long names wrap onto up to three lines. Prefer roles over personal names.

tasks.description: The rows, top to bottom (1–30): tasks, deliverables or decisions, each with one cell per role. A row with "type": "section" is a full-width phase heading (e.g. "Discovery") that groups the tasks below it; it has no cells.

cells.description: One cell per role, in the same order as `roles`: "R" Responsible (does the work), "A" Accountable (owns it and signs off; exactly one per task), "C" Consulted (two-way input), "I" Informed (kept up to date), "S" Support (RASCI only: helps the R), "A/R" for an owner who also does the work, or "" for blank. Lowercase and "R/A" are accepted. A shorter array leaves the remaining cells blank, a longer one is truncated; anything else is left blank with a warning.

name.description: Task or section name, e.g. "Approve the budget" or "Discovery". Keep tasks to a short verb phrase; long names wrap onto two lines, then truncate.

type.description: Omit for a normal task row. "section" draws a full-width phase heading instead; its cells are ignored.

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400, default 1280, which suits a 16:9 slide). PNG output renders at 2x. Height is computed from the content.

inputSchema.title: RACI Matrix
